title: College Grads And AI
gist: An expert panel (Cadence, Synopsys, Southampton University, llmda.ai, Breker, ChipAgents) says AI coding tools are slowing CS/data-science hiring and displacing intern-level work, but chip design remains talent-short so EE demand holds. Panelists warn that cutting junior hiring and mentoring risks a future expertise gap, while noting recent grads are now the in-house AI experts.

insights.claim: Cadence fellow Chuck Alpert says vibe-coding tools such as Cursor, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot are raising programmer productivity, and companies spending heavily on Claude and OpenAI are hiring fewer engineers as a result.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: AI coding tool spend is substituting for headcount, supporting AI vendor revenue at the expense of software labor demand.
insights.quote: Companies are spending a lot of money on Claude and OpenAI for these things, and they don’t want to hire quite so many engineers at quite the same rate.
insights.locator: Alpert: We know that the vibe-coding tools

insights.claim: llmda.ai CEO Nagesh Gupta says data science graduates are far more affected by AI than computer science graduates, and good CS grads from strong universities remain scarce.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Suggests AI labor displacement is uneven across technical disciplines.
insights.locator: Gupta: From my observations, data science

insights.claim: Southampton University's Simon Davidmann cites UK data showing graduate recruitment among leading employers fell 24% from 2022 to 2026, attributed mainly to economic uncertainty, budget cuts and post-pandemic corrections rather than AI, while about 75% of engineering grads find jobs within 15 months.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Cautions against over-attributing weak graduate labor markets to AI; macro factors dominate.
insights.locator: Davidmann: I did some digging around

insights.claim: Breker CEO Dave Kelf says AI is replacing the need for interns and junior tasks once used for training, and firms feel they cannot afford new grads if competitors use AI instead, creating a profitability-driven squeeze on entry-level hiring.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Competitive pressure accelerates AI substitution for junior labor across engineering firms.
insights.quote: If we hire them and our competitors are using AI, then we have a problem with profitability versus our competitors.
insights.locator: Kelf: I ran AI to ask this question

insights.claim: Synopsys VP Thomas Andersen says chip designers have been in shortage for a long time and AI is helping address it by elevating tasks rather than removing humans, with the goal of halving time to tape out chips.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Positions AI-enabled EDA as a productivity product with strong demand from talent-constrained chipmakers.
insights.locator: Andersen: When we talk about computer scientists

insights.claim: Alpert says designs are roughly 10x more complex due to packaging, 3D-ICs and multi-physics verification with the same timeframes, so even 10x more productive designers will not close the gap and there will never be a shortage of demand for EEs.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Sustained design complexity growth underpins long-run EDA demand including AI agent tools.
insights.quote: The number of designs people want to do means there’s never going to be a shortage of EE’s, even if designers are 10× more productive.
insights.locator: Alpert: There’s such a huge productivity gap

insights.claim: EDA industry insiders claim current AI agents are as good as junior engineers, with senior engineers expected to manage around 10 agents, described as virtual engineers.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Agentic EDA could be priced per virtual engineer, expanding EDA vendors' monetizable market.
insights.locator: SE: It has been said that this won’t affect

insights.claim: Davidmann and Andersen warn that cutting graduate hiring because AI handles simple tasks will create a long-term expertise gap as current experts age, a gap AI will not fill.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Long-dated risk to semiconductor engineering capacity if firms underinvest in junior talent.
insights.quote: if I don’t replace the existing experts, who’s ever going to do it?
insights.locator: Davidmann: That is a short-term problem

insights.claim: Gupta relays that at a large company, senior staff using AI no longer make time to mentor new grads, prompting the company to form a focus group to address onboarding.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: An early sign of organizational friction from AI adoption that may reduce workforce development.
insights.locator: Gupta: From my own experience, my daughter

insights.claim: ChipAgents' Kexun Zhang says companies now expect new grads to be AI-native and solve higher-level problems with taste and initiative, but university education cannot adapt fast enough, leaving recent graduates in a gap.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Skills mismatch creates demand for AI-native training and reskilling products.
insights.locator: Zhang: There is a big mismatch

insights.claim: Davidmann proposes splitting engineering education into a foundation mode without AI (math, algorithms, debugging) and a professional mode using agents as part of the job.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Signals how EDA vendors' university programs may evolve to include AI tooling.
insights.locator: Davidmann: Being back in the university scene

themes.theme: Junior engineers as AI adoption leaders

insights.claim: Alpert says engineers hired within the last two years are among Cadence's best sources of AI expertise, reversing the usual knowledge flow from senior to junior staff.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: AI adoption speed inside EDA firms may depend on younger staff overcoming senior resistance.
insights.quote: Three to five years ago, if I had asked what a young engineer could teach me, the answer would have been nothing.
insights.locator: Alpert: I’m finding that a lot

insights.claim: Kelf compares AI to earlier EDA waves such as logic synthesis and randomized verification, where new grads trained in HDLs and object-oriented test benches drove adoption over resistant senior engineers.
insights.speaker: Brian Bailey
insights.so_what: Historical pattern implies AI EDA adoption will accelerate as AI-native cohorts enter the workforce.
insights.locator: Kelf: There have been waves within EDA
